guard: The version-2 entry's host seam: a failure that crosses the thread boundary is rehydrated into the class drive() grades (L5010 as JournalAppendRejected, L5012 as RunReleased), and the host's stop conditions reach the run at the walker's own granularity - before the first effect when the horizon predates the run, and at every effect boundary after, riding the append rather than a timer.
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/engine-host.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd

mutations.name: a lost journal crosses back as a plain error rather than the class the driver grades
mutations.expectRed: the superseded driver is RELEASED, not completed and not thrown
mutations.cell: the superseded driver is RELEASED, not completed and not thrown
mutations.note: drive() grades a lost run by instanceof, and instanceof does not survive a thread boundary - the rehydration map is what puts the class back. Mutated, a superseded driver's L5010 arrives as a generic error, drive() rethrows it as a run failure, and a run somebody else now owns is recorded as failed by a process that no longer speaks for it.

mutations.name: a release crosses back as a failure
mutations.expectRed: a driver past its work horizon RELEASES the run rather than failing it
mutations.cell: a driver past its work horizon RELEASES the run rather than failing it
mutations.note: The host stopping is not a fact about the program, and the outcome contract says so as `released`. Mutated, the thread's RunReleased crosses as a plain error, drive() records `failed` onto a run that neither failed nor finished, and the next driver reads a terminal state about work that is still resumable.

mutations.name: the stop rides only the timer, not the append boundary
mutations.expectRed: it stopped BETWEEN effects, not before the run and not after it: exactly one effects
mutations.cell: it stopped BETWEEN effects, not before the run and not after it: exactly one effects
mutations.note: Every effect is bracketed by durable appends, so the check riding the append is what gives the engine the walker's own between-effects granularity. Mutated, only the 100ms timer is left, a millisecond-scale run finishes before its first tick, and a driver past its horizon performs the second effect the walker would have refused.

mutations.name: a horizon that predates the run is noticed only at the first append
mutations.find:
const already = req.shouldStop();
  if (already !== undefined) worker.stop(already);
mutations.replace:
const already = undefined as string | undefined;
  if (already !== undefined) worker.stop(already);
mutations.expectRed: a horizon already past at the start stops the run before its first effect
mutations.cell: a horizon already past at the start stops the run before its first effect
mutations.note: The thread's first pre-effect check reads the shared flag; a stop published on the pending APPEND arrives after that check has passed, so the first effect runs. The walker answers this case with zero effects, and the upfront publish is the one line that makes the engine give the same answer.

mutations.name: a throwing stop check crashes the host from the poll's timer stack
mutations.expectRed: a stop check that throws on the poll's own stack is the RUN'S fault, never an uncaught exception
mutations.cell: a stop check that throws on the poll's own stack is the RUN'S fault, never an uncaught exception
mutations.note: Rethrowing from the timer callback is exactly the unguarded shape this guard replaced: the throw lands on Timeout._onTimeout, bypasses the driver's catch, and without the cell's own uncaughtException trap it kills the host process (MEASURED at c24be213). The cell traps the escape so the kill is a named red rather than a dead suite. The stop check throws ONCE: a throw on every tick, after the listener is removed, killed the process before `run-driver.smoke:` and graded INCONCLUSIVE (measured at d4033944).

mutations.name: the poll ticks but reads nothing, so a stop with no append traffic is never heard
mutations.find:
const reason = req.shouldStop();
      if (reason !== undefined) worker.stop(reason);
mutations.expectRed: a stop only the poll can see, raised inside a parked effect with no append traffic, still stops the run at the next effect
mutations.cell: a stop only the poll can see, raised inside a parked effect with no append traffic, still stops the run at the next effect
mutations.note: The timer's one load-bearing window, measured: a stop true only while an effect is parked in the host reaches the run through no other path, because the append boundaries on either side of the park see the flag lowered. Neutered, the run completes and performs the second effect the stop should have prevented. Every other suite stayed green under this mutant before the cell existed.

unkillable.name: the worker entry's existence check reaches for a fallback path
unkillable.why: `resolveWorkerEntry` refuses a missing dist artifact by name. Ungradable from this suite because the suite cannot run at all without the artifact the check guards: `smoke:lang-engine` builds it and every honest run of this config has it on disk, so a mutant deleting the existence check is a no-op at its own program point and could only report SURVIVED. The refusal text is held by the code beside a comment naming the build step; the day a fixture can stage a missing dist without breaking the suite's own imports, this belongs in the set above.
